results.q: How does the vehicle decide which way to steer?
answer: motor_set_steering() has no code in this project — it is an output (hardware/OS output (by name)) (hal/hal.h:8). The decision is made by the code that calls it:
VehicleController_SetDirection() (control/vehicle_controller.c:10) — Converts the heading error into a rate-limited steering command and sends it to the motor.

Step by step, it calls wrap180() and stores the result in `error` (line 12); then it calls clamp() and stores the result in `command` (line 13); then it calls clamp() and stores the result in `command` (line 17); then it sets `s_last_command_deg = command` (line 18); then it calls motor_set_steering() (line 19).

It is called by NavigationTick() at nav/navigation.c:81 with (`currentHeading`, `target_heading`) — `target_heading = bearing_deg(g_nav.latitude, g_nav.longitude, g_nav.target_lat, g_nav.target_lon)` (line 80), only when `g_nav.has_fix && (now_ms - g_nav.last_fix_ms) > GPS_TIMEOUT_MS` is false (GPS_TIMEOUT_MS = 2000), only when `g_nav.mode != NAV_MODE_TRACKING && g_nav.mode != NAV_MODE_DEAD_RECKONING` is false (NAV_MODE_TRACKING = 1, NAV_MODE_DEAD_RECKONING = 4). The full chain from the program's start is: main() → NavigationTick() → VehicleController_SetDirection().
VehicleController_Hold() (control/vehicle_controller.c:23) — Centres the steering and signals that the route is no longer being followed.
Step by step, it sets `s_last_command_deg = 0.0` (line 25); then it calls motor_set_steering() (line 26); then it calls led_set_status() (line 27).

It is called by NavigationTick() at nav/navigation.c:73, only when `g_nav.has_fix && (now_ms - g_nav.last_fix_ms) > GPS_TIMEOUT_MS` is true (GPS_TIMEOUT_MS = 2000). The full chain from the program's start is: main() → NavigationTick() → VehicleController_Hold().
The values it updates are used later by VehicleController_SetDirection() (uses s_last_command_deg).

results.q: Where is the ring buffer filled?
answer: ring_buffer_t is written by: rb_init() (head, tail; drivers/ring_buffer.c:5); rb_push() (data, head; drivers/ring_buffer.c:17); rb_pop() (tail; drivers/ring_buffer.c:29).

rb_push(): It is called by USART2_IRQHandler() at drivers/uart_isr.c:12 with (`&g_gps_rx`, `byte`) — `uint8_t byte = (uint8_t)(USART2->DR & 0xFFu)` (line 11), only when `USART2->SR & USART_SR_RXNE` is true. The full chain from the program's start is: USART2_IRQHandler() → rb_push().
rb_init(): It is called by gps_receiver_init() at gps/gps_receiver.c:35 with (`&g_gps_rx`). The full chain from the program's start is: main() → gps_receiver_init() → rb_init().
rb_pop(): It is called by gps_receiver_poll() at gps/gps_receiver.c:109 with (`&g_gps_rx`, `&byte`). The full chain from the program's start is: main() → gps_receiver_poll() → rb_pop().

results.q: What calls NavigationTick and how often?
answer: It is called by main() at app/main.c:25 with (`now`) — `uint32_t now = hal_get_tick_ms()` (line 20), repeatedly inside `for (;;)`, only when `(now - last_tick) >= NAV_TICK_MS` is true (NAV_TICK_MS = 100). The full chain from the program's start is: main() → NavigationTick().

results.q: Trace the speed value from the GPS sentence to where it is used
answer: gps_fix_t.speed_knots (field, include/gps_types.h:10) — "speed over ground, knots".
It is assigned by `fix.speed_knots = atof(s->fields[6])` in handle_rmc() (gps/gps_receiver.c:69).
`s` is a parameter of handle_rmc(): gps_receiver_process_line() passes `&sentence` (gps/gps_receiver.c:97).

Tracing back further, the value originates at DR (input: memory-mapped register) and travels: USART2_IRQHandler() → rb_push() → rb_pop() → gps_receiver_poll() → gps_receiver_process_line() → nmea_split() → handle_rmc() → gps_fix_t.speed_knots.
It is copied into nav_state_t.speed_knots by ProcessGpsData() (`g_nav.speed_knots = fix->speed_knots`, nav/navigation.c:56).
ProcessGpsData() passes it to CalculateHeading() (`fix->speed_knots`, nav/navigation.c:59).
Where it is used: ProcessGpsData().

results.q: What happens when the GPS reports only 3 satellites?
answer: I ran the real code in a sandbox with satellites = 3.
Functions that ran, in order: ProcessGpsData() → gps_validate_fix() → nav_handle_invalid_fix() → NavigationTick().

Decisions, in the order they ran: in ProcessGpsData(): `status != GPS_OK` was TRUE (line 49); in gps_validate_fix(): `fix == 0 || !fix->valid` was false (line 7), `fix->latitude < -90.0 || fix->latitude > 90.0 || fix->longitude < -180.0 || fix->longitude > 180.0` was false (line 10), `fix->hdop > GPS_MAX_HDOP || fix->satellites < GPS_MIN_SATELLITES` was TRUE (line 14); in nav_handle_invalid_fix(): `g_nav.consecutive_invalid >= MAX_INVALID_FIXES` was false (line 25); in NavigationTick(): `g_nav.has_fix && (now_ms - g_nav.last_fix_ms) > GPS_TIMEOUT_MS` was false (line 68), `g_nav.mode != NAV_MODE_TRACKING && g_nav.mode != NAV_MODE_DEAD_RECKONING` was TRUE (line 77).
Resulting values: g_nav.consecutive_invalid = 1.
It did not call any output functions (hal_get_tick_ms(), led_set_status(), motor_set_steering() were not called).
The best match is nmea_parse_coord() (gps/nmea_parser.c:61).
nmea_parse_coord() (gps/nmea_parser.c:61) — Converts NMEA "ddmm.mmmm" plus hemisphere into signed decimal degrees.

Step by step, it calls atof() and stores the result in `raw` (line 63); then it sets `int degrees = (int)(raw / 100.0)` (line 64); then it sets `double minutes = raw - (double)degrees * 100.0` (line 65); then it sets `double result = (double)degrees + minutes / 60.0` (line 66); then it checks `hemisphere[0] == 'S' || hemisphere[0] == 'W'` (line 68); if true it sets `result = -result`; then it returns `result` (line 71).

It is called by handle_rmc() at gps/gps_receiver.c:67 with (`s->fields[2]`, `s->fields[3]`), only when `s->field_count < 8` is false; handle_rmc() at gps/gps_receiver.c:68 with (`s->fields[4]`, `s->fields[5]`), only when `s->field_count < 8` is false. The full chain from the program's start is: main() → gps_receiver_poll() → gps_receiver_process_line() → handle_rmc() → nmea_parse_coord().
Other candidates: nmea_split() (gps/nmea_parser.c:33).
nav_handle_invalid_fix() (nav/navigation.c:22) — Counts consecutive bad fixes; too many switches navigation to degraded mode.

Step by step, it sets `g_nav.consecutive_invalid++` (line 24); then it checks `g_nav.consecutive_invalid >= MAX_INVALID_FIXES` (MAX_INVALID_FIXES = 5) (line 25); if true it sets `g_nav.mode = NAV_MODE_DEGRADED`.

It is called by ProcessGpsData() at nav/navigation.c:50 with (`status`) — `gps_status_t status = gps_validate_fix(fix)` (line 47), only when `status != GPS_OK` is true (GPS_OK = 0). The full chain from the program's start is: main() → gps_receiver_poll() → gps_receiver_process_line() → handle_rmc() → ProcessGpsData() → nav_handle_invalid_fix().
The values it updates are used later by NavigationTick() (uses nav_state_t.mode).
bearing_deg() (nav/geo_math.c:31) — Initial great-circle bearing from point 1 to point 2, degrees true.

Step by step, it sets `double p1 = lat1 * PI / 180.0` (line 33); then it sets `double p2 = lat2 * PI / 180.0` (line 34); then it sets `double dl = (lon2 - lon1) * PI / 180.0` (line 35); then it calls sin() and stores the result in `y` (line 36); then it calls cos() and stores the result in `x` (line 37); then it calls wrap360() (line 39); then it returns `wrap360(atan2(y, x) * 180.0 / PI)` (line 39).

It is called by NavigationTick() at nav/navigation.c:80 with (`g_nav.latitude`, `g_nav.longitude`, `g_nav.target_lat`, `g_nav.target_lon`), only when `g_nav.has_fix && (now_ms - g_nav.last_fix_ms) > GPS_TIMEOUT_MS` is false (GPS_TIMEOUT_MS = 2000), only when `g_nav.mode != NAV_MODE_TRACKING && g_nav.mode != NAV_MODE_DEAD_RECKONING` is false (NAV_MODE_TRACKING = 1, NAV_MODE_DEAD_RECKONING = 4). The full chain from the program's start is: main() → NavigationTick() → bearing_deg().

results.q: What would break if I removed wrap360?
answer: Changing wrap360() (nav/geo_math.c:7) can affect three kinds of things: the code that calls it, the data that depends on its result, and the outputs that data reaches.

Called directly by: CalculateHeading(), wrap180(), bearing_deg(). Indirectly (through the call chain): ProcessGpsData(), VehicleController_SetDirection(), NavigationTick(), handle_rmc(), main(), gps_receiver_process_line(), gps_receiver_poll().
Its result is stored in CalculateHeading() result, wrap180() result, bearing_deg() result (nav/navigation.c:41, nav/geo_math.c:20, nav/geo_math.c:39).
Functions that use values derived from it: CalculateHeading(), NavigationTick(), VehicleController_SetDirection(), bearing_deg(), clamp(), wrap180().
Through that data it can ultimately change what is sent to motor_set_steering() (hardware/OS output (by name)) — a change in wrap360() can change the physical output.
It runs on this path from the program start: main() → NavigationTick() → bearing_deg() → wrap360().
g_fix_callback is a global variable of type `gps_fix_callback_t`, defined in gps/gps_receiver.c:11.
It is set by gps_receiver_set_callback() (`g_fix_callback = cb`, line 43).
It is read by handle_rmc() (line 75).
g_fix_callback holds a function: at run time it points to ProcessGpsData() (registered at app/main.c:16); it is called by handle_rmc().
In short: g_fix_callback carries a value produced by gps_receiver_set_callback() and consumed by handle_rmc().

results.q: When does the LED turn off?
answer: These parts of the code look most relevant: led_set_status() (function, hal/hal.h:9); main() (function, app/main.c:10); gps_validate_fix() (function, gps/gps_validation.c:5); MAX_TURN_RATE_DEG (constant, include/nav_config.h:10); VehicleController_Hold() (function, control/vehicle_controller.c:23); NavigationTick() (function, nav/navigation.c:64).
led_set_status() (hal/hal.h:9) — status LED.

results.q: What happens when the GPS fix quality is too low?
answer: This is handled in GpsService.OnFix() (src/Services/GpsService.cs:32): it checks `Enabled && fix.Quality >= _options.MinQuality`, and when that is true it checks `_controller.ProcessGpsData(fix)` (line 34); if true it calls Interlocked.Increment and sets `Interlocked.Increment(ref _accepted)`; then it calls NavigationController.ProcessGpsData() (line 34); then it calls Interlocked.Increment (line 37).
When it does not return there, GpsService.OnFix() goes on to call Interlocked.Increment with (`ref _rejected`) (line 41).

NavigationController.ProcessGpsData() sets `_state.RejectedFixes++` (line 42); then it sets `_state.RejectedFixes++` (line 48); then it sets `double speedMps = fix.SpeedKnots * NmeaParser.KnotsToMetersPerSecond` (line 52); then it checks `_previousFixUtc == DateTime.MinValue` (line 56); then it sets `double dt = _previousFixUtc == DateTime.MinValue ? 0.0 : (fix.TimestampUtc - _previousFixUtc).TotalSeconds` (line 56); then it sets `_previousFixUtc = fix.TimestampUtc` (line 59).

Consequence: NavLoop.Tick() checks `_state.Mode == NavMode.Initializing` (src/Control/NavLoop.cs:30); `_state.Mode == NavMode.Initializing` depends on runtime values, so it may return early, skipping PidController.Reset(), GeoMath.Wrap180(), PidController.Update().

Consequence: NavLoop.Tick() checks `now - _state.LastFixUtc > _options.StaleFixTimeout` (src/Control/NavLoop.cs:33); `now - _state.LastFixUtc > _options.StaleFixTimeout` depends on runtime values, so it may call PidController.Reset().

Consequence: NavLoop.Tick() checks `_state.Mode != NavMode.DeadReckoning` (src/Control/NavLoop.cs:35); `_state.Mode != NavMode.DeadReckoning` depends on runtime values, so it may call PidController.Reset().

results.q: How does the bank command reach the autopilot?
answer: I could not trace a complete path from an input to an output for this topic; here is the central function instead.
AutopilotLink.SendBankCommand() (src/Control/AutopilotLink.cs:72) — Sends a bank command in degrees (positive = right wing down).

Step by step, it calls Double.IsNaN (line 74); then it calls ArgumentOutOfRangeException.#ctor (line 75); then it calls AutopilotLink.FormatFrame() (line 77); then it calls Encoding.GetBytes (line 78); then it calls AutopilotTransport.Send() (line 79).

It is called by NavLoop.Tick() at src/Control/NavLoop.cs:54 with (`bank`) — `double bank = _pid.Update(error, dt)` (line 43), only when `_state.Mode == NavMode.Initializing` is false. The full chain from the program's start is: lambda() → NavLoop.Tick() → AutopilotLink.SendBankCommand().
The values it updates are used later by CommandsSent.get() (uses AutopilotLink._sequence).

These parts of the code look most relevant: SerialGpsSensor.FixReceived (event, src/Sensors/SerialGpsSensor.cs:20); SerialGpsSensor.OnFixReceived() (method, src/Sensors/SerialGpsSensor.cs:73); GpsService.Dispose() (method, src/Services/GpsService.cs:45); GpsService.OnFix() (method, src/Services/GpsService.cs:29); GpsFixEventArgs (class, src/Model/GpsFix.cs:47); SerialGpsSensor.HandleLine() (method, src/Sensors/SerialGpsSensor.cs:40).
NavLoop.Tick() (src/Control/NavLoop.cs:25) — One control step; called by a timer at ~10 Hz.

Step by step, it checks `_lastTick == DateTime.MinValue` (line 27); then it sets `double dt = _lastTick == DateTime.MinValue ? 0.0 : (now - _lastTick).TotalSeconds` (line 27); then it sets `_lastTick = now` (line 28); then it checks `now - _state.LastFixUtc > _options.StaleFixTimeout` (line 33); if true it calls PidController.Reset() and sets `_state.Mode = NavMode.DeadReckoning`; then it checks `_state.Mode != NavMode.DeadReckoning` (line 35); if true it calls PidController.Reset() and sets `_state.Mode = NavMode.DeadReckoning`; then it calls GeoMath.Wrap180() and stores the result in `error` (line 42); then it calls PidController.Update() (line 43); then it checks `bank > _options.MaxBankDeg` (line 45); if true it sets `bank = _options.MaxBankDeg`; then it checks `bank < -_options.MaxBankDeg` (line 47); if true it sets `bank = -_options.MaxBankDeg`; then it checks `_state.Mode == NavMode.DeadReckoning` (line 50); then it calls AutopilotLink.SendBankCommand() (line 54); ….
It is called by lambda() at src/Program.cs:38 with (`DateTime.UtcNow`). The full chain from the program's start is: lambda() → NavLoop.Tick().
